question: What four crosswalk marking patterns are illustrated in Figure 3C-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3C-1 illustrates four crosswalk marking patterns: (1) Transverse, consisting of two parallel transverse lines, and three high-visibility designs — (2) Longitudinal Bar, (3) Ladder, and (4) Bar Pair. The transverse design is the basic pattern, while the longitudinal bar, ladder, and bar pair designs make up the high-visibility category. Guidance (recommended): - "Transverse line crosswalk markings should be limited to locations controlled by traffic control signals or on approaches controlled by STOP or YIELD signs." Visual evidence: - [Image 6] shows Figure 3C-1 "Crosswalk Markings" on page 590, labeling the four patterns — Transverse, and the High-Visibility group of Longitudinal Bar, Ladder, and Bar Pair — along with dimensional details (e.g., transverse lines 6 to 24 inches wide, longitudinal bars 12 to 24 inches wide, 6 ft minimum crosswalk width). - [Image 8] shows page 591 (Sections 3C.04 and 3C.05), which explains that transverse line design consists of two parallel transverse lines and that high-visibility crosswalk markings include the longitudinal bar, ladder, and bar pair designs, all cross-referenced to Figure 3C-1. Citations: - Section 3C.04 Guidance §1 (p.591) - Page 631 - Page 632
gold_answer: Transverse, longitudinal bar, ladder, and bar pair.
